## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed before merge: `--exclude` does not read its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the project's CLI-flags policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. The pattern matching and its wiring into `collect` and `main` are correct, and the added tests cover them.

## Changes
Adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that drops files from the archive when their basename matches any of the patterns, and logs each skipped path at info level. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If you run with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` flag, nothing is excluded, because the default is hard-coded as `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so those archives will include files the jobs meant to skip. — Fix: Take the default from `os.environ` (for example, split `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` on a separator you document), add a test next to `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`, and list the variable in `docs/flags.md`.
